newsitem.title: USA: Newspaper says Sen. John Glenn to retire.
newsitem.headline: Newspaper says Sen. John Glenn to retire.

text.p: Four-term Democratic Sen. John Glenn has decided not to seek re-election next year, it was reported Tuesday.
The 75-year-old space hero will make the announcement in Ohio later this week, the Plain-Dealer newspaper said, citing Democratic party sources.

Glenn's office in Washington refused to confirm the story, but said Glenn would announce whether or not he was running for another term Thursday afternoon in a speech in his home town of New Concord, Ohio, at his alma mater, Muskingum College.

Glenn, who in 1962 became the first American to orbit the earth, was first elected to the Senate in 1974 and is the only Ohioan ever elected to four Senate terms. He unsuccessfully sought his party's presidential nomination in 1984.

The newspaper said his decision was "not unexpected yet Democrats as high up as President Clinton held up hope that Glenn would run once again to protect a seat regarded as vulnerable to a Republican challenge."
Republican Gov. George Voinovich, who is not eligible for a third consecutive gubernatorial term under Ohio law, has been widely reported ready to seek the Republican nomination for Glenn's seat.
Potential Democratic hopefuls include Cleveland lawyer Joel Hyatt, Cuyahoga County Commissioner Mary Boyle and U.S. Representative Sherrod Brown of Lorain.
